events.title: WorldWideWeb — first web browser
events.summary: Tim Berners-Lee finished the WorldWideWeb browser and editor at CERN in December 1990 — the first program to browse hyperlinked documents over the internet.
events.about: WorldWideWeb ran on NeXT workstations and let researchers open linked pages, edit them, and follow citations — the prototype for every browser that followed. It introduced URLs, clickable links, and the idea that documents on different servers could form one web.

narrative.whyChosen: This is the origin point of the web as a browsable medium, not just a file-transfer network.
narrative.whyImportant: It proved hypertext could work across the internet and gave the web its first user interface.
narrative.problemSolved: CERN scientists needed a practical way to navigate and share linked documentation across machines and projects.
